pharm: Beta-lactam antibiotic; inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis
summary: Cephalexin is a first-generation oral cephalosporin used for susceptible respiratory tract, skin, bone, otitis media, and genitourinary infections. It is generally well tolerated, with diarrhea the most common adverse effect. Cross-hypersensitivity may occur in up to 10% of penicillin-allergic patients, and dose reduction is required in severe renal impairment.
indications: Respiratory tract infections (S. pneumoniae, S. pyogenes)
Otitis media (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, S. aureus, S. pyogenes, M. catarrhalis)
Skin and skin structure infections (S. aureus, S. pyogenes)
Genitourinary tract infections including acute prostatitis (E. coli, P. mirabilis, K. pneumoniae)

dosage.c: Adults and patients at least 15 years of age
dosage.d: 250 mg every 6 hours, or 500 mg every 12 hours
dosage.n: For more severe infections up to 4 g/day in 2-4 divided doses

dosage.c: Pediatric patients over 1 year - all indications except otitis media
dosage.d: 25 to 50 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses
dosage.n: Beta-hemolytic streptococcal infections: at least 10 days

dosage.c: Pediatric patients over 1 year - severe infections
dosage.d: 50 to 100 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses

dosage.c: Pediatric patients over 1 year - otitis media
dosage.d: 75 to 100 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses

dosage.c: Renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min), >=15 years of age
dosage.n: Insufficient data to recommend in pediatric patients with renal impairment

admin: Acid stable; may be given without regard to meals
Complete the full prescribed course even if symptoms improve
Space doses evenly across the day
moa: Cephalexin is a beta-lactam (cephalosporin) antibacterial that inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis, producing a bactericidal effect against susceptible organisms.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to cephalexin or other cephalosporin-class antibacterials
relative: History of penicillin or other beta-lactam allergy (cross-hypersensitivity in up to 10%)
monitor: Patients with renal impairment (longer monitoring for toxicity and drug interactions due to delayed clearance)

preg: Available epidemiologic and pharmacovigilance data over several decades have not established a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal/fetal outcomes; animal studies (0.6-1.2x MRHD) showed no fetal harm.
lact: Present in human milk with a Relative Infant Dose <1% of the maternal weight-adjusted dose; weigh benefits of breastfeeding against maternal need and potential infant effects. Generally considered compatible.
renal: Dose adjustment is required in severe and end-stage renal disease (CrCl <30 mL/min). Monitor patients with renal impairment longer for toxicity and drug interactions; use a lower dose to reduce seizure potential.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment specified. Transient hepatitis and cholestatic jaundice have been reported.

moderate: Metformin (increased metformin concentrations - monitor for hypoglycemia and adjust metformin dose)
Probenecid (inhibits renal excretion of cephalexin - co-administration not recommended)
interactions.food: May be administered with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction stated in the label.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause a false-positive urine glucose reaction with Benedict's or Fehling's solution; direct Coombs' test seroconversion may occur.

serious: Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea (up to fatal colitis)

monitoring: Evaluate for C. difficile-associated diarrhea if diarrhea develops
Evaluate for drug-induced hemolytic anemia if anemia develops during/after therapy (direct Coombs' test)
Renal function, especially in elderly and renally impaired patients
Blood glucose in patients also taking metformin
counsel: Complete the full prescribed course even if you feel better
Inform your clinician of any prior allergy to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics
Report persistent or bloody diarrhea, which can occur even weeks after therapy
Stop the drug and seek care immediately for rash, hives, swelling, or breathing difficulty
May be taken with or without food
pk: Serum peak ~1 hour (approx. 9, 18, 32 mcg/mL after 250 mg, 500 mg, 1 g)
Serum levels detectable up to 6 hours after a dose
Store per product labeling (capsules in bottle)
pearls: Cross-hypersensitivity among beta-lactams may occur in up to 10% of patients with penicillin allergy
>90% excreted unchanged in urine within 8 hours - accumulation drives dose reduction in renal impairment and seizure risk
Acid stable, so absorption is unaffected by food; convenient for once- or twice-daily compliance with q12h dosing
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Symptoms may include nausea, vomiting, epigastric distress, diarrhea, and hematuria. Institute general supportive measures. Forced diuresis, peritoneal dialysis, hemodialysis, or charcoal hemoperfusion have not been established as beneficial.
